raw_evidence.quote: The entity model below captures the minimum persisted structures needed to realise the PRD goals and the engineering rules in spec-draft.md. The ERD is the conceptual model; physical schemas may split large payload fields or use partitions.

composite_primary_keys.rationale: The incumbent marks BOTH columns of each intended composite key with the PK label (e.g. task_version_id PK and sequence_no PK on OUTCOME_RULE). Per source-mermaid-erd-syntax.json and source-mermaid-erd-grammar.json, this is exactly the documented per-attribute PK label used twice, with no composite-key grouping semantic in the language — the diagram renders two PK badges, not one composite-key construct. The prose does not separately restate these as composite keys either; the fact of compositeness is implicit and must be inferred by a reader from the double-PK pattern.

json_payload_columns.citation: erDiagram block, TASK_VERSION entity (schedule_spec, window_spec, dependency_spec, output_condition_spec, retry_spec, cyclic_spec all typed 'json')
json_payload_columns.rationale: Expressed directly IN the diagram as free-text type labels, consistent with source-mermaid-erd-syntax.json's finding that 'json' is accepted as an ordinary type token with no structural validation attached.

enumerated_string_domains.citation: FOLDER_RUN.execution_context typed 'string' in the diagram (line 117) versus prose constraint 20 stating the SCHEDULED|MANUAL domain; NAMED_RESOURCE_LINK.link_kind typed 'string' in the diagram (line 137) versus prose constraint 17 stating the HOST_CAPACITY|NAMED_RESOURCE domain
enumerated_string_domains.rationale: Both enumerated domains named in the research plan are entirely absent from the diagram itself — the diagram shows only the generic type 'string' with no hint of a constrained value set — and are stated exclusively in prose. This is a direct, confirmed instance of the split the task asked to establish precisely.

self_referencing_foreign_keys_multiple.citation: TASK_INSTANCE attribute block (three FK-marked columns, lines ~161-163) versus only two self-referencing relationship lines drawn (lines 290-291)
self_referencing_foreign_keys_multiple.rationale: All three FK columns (origin_instance_id, cyclic_root_instance_id, previous_iteration_id) ARE declared as attributes with the FK label, so column-level declaration is complete. But only two relationship lines are drawn ('reruns' and 'cyclic_predecessor'), covering origin_instance_id and one of the cyclic-lineage columns; no third relationship line distinguishes cyclic_root_instance_id from previous_iteration_id — they appear to share the single 'cyclic_predecessor' edge, or one of the three FK columns has no corresponding drawn edge at all. Per source-mermaid-erd-grammar.json this is not a language limitation (three distinct self-referencing relationship lines are legal), so this is an authoring choice/gap in the incumbent, not a Mermaid ceiling — but it is exactly the imprecision the research plan asked to establish.

nullable_foreign_keys.citation: TASK_INSTANCE.folder_run_id and TASK_INSTANCE.plan_id, both typed 'uuid FK' with no nullability marker in the diagram, versus prose constraint 06 stating folder_run_id is nullable and constraint 07 implying plan_id is null for reruns
nullable_foreign_keys.rationale: The diagram was authored before (or without using) Mermaid's v11.16.0 optional-type-suffix feature documented in source-mermaid-erd-syntax.json; nullability for these two FKs is stated only in prose, not in the diagram, even though the upstream language now has a way to express it.

multi_column_unique_constraints.citation: PLAN and NAMED_RESOURCE entities in the diagram carry no UK marking on domain_id or odate/name, versus prose constraints 04 and 15 stating the (domain_id, odate) and (domain_id, name) uniqueness
multi_column_unique_constraints.rationale: Confirms the task's framing precisely: these two multi-column UNIQUE constraints exist ONLY in the numbered prose constraints beneath the diagram, not in the erDiagram block itself in any form (not even via the UK label or a comment workaround).

one_to_zero_or_one_relationships.citation: erDiagram block, line 294: ATTEMPT ||--o| ATTEMPT_RESULT : accepts
one_to_zero_or_one_relationships.rationale: Expressed directly and correctly IN the diagram using Mermaid's documented cardinality notation — the one advanced construct in this survey that the incumbent both needs and already renders natively without any workaround or prose fallback.

value_constraint_beyond_type.citation: NAMED_RESOURCE_LINK.resource_task_weight typed plain 'string' in the diagram (line 138) versus prose constraint 16 stating the decimal-positive-integer-or-literal-ALL rule
value_constraint_beyond_type.rationale: The diagram cannot even hint at the disjunctive constraint through its type token (it falls back to the generic 'string' type, losing even the numeric hint); the entire rule, including the cross-field constraint against concurrency_limit, is carried in prose constraint 16.

several_logical_schemas_in_one_database.citation: Entire erDiagram block — all 25 entities appear in one flat, ungrouped diagram with no schema/namespace markers, and the prose constraints likewise never group entities by schema
several_logical_schemas_in_one_database.rationale: No trace of a configuration/runtime/audit/resources split anywhere in this artifact, consistent with source-mermaid-erd-syntax.json and source-mermaid-erd-grammar.json's finding that erDiagram has no such construct at all.

cross_cutting_validator_convention.citation: Entire file — domain_id FK appears repeatedly by hand-authored repetition (DOMAIN, TASK_DEFINITION, FOLDER_DEFINITION, PLAN, FOLDER_RUN, TASK_INSTANCE, NAMED_RESOURCE, WORKLOAD_POLICY, OPERATOR_INTENT, AGENT all carry a domain_id FK line) with no assertion anywhere that this convention holds for every Domain-owned table
cross_cutting_validator_convention.rationale: The convention is only as reliable as manual authoring discipline; nothing in the file or the Mermaid toolchain would catch a future entity that forgets domain_id. This is the concrete instance of the 'silent drift' risk named in the research brief's cost_of_error.

contrary_evidence_search.result: Confirmed by direct reading (not search-engine query, since this is a local in-repo file): of the ten advanced constructs, only JSON payload columns and the one-to-zero-or-one relationship are fully expressed inside the diagram itself. Composite primary keys and self-referencing FK columns are partially expressed (attribute-level labels present, but without composite/complete-relationship semantics). Enumerated domains, nullable FKs, multi-column UNIQUE constraints, and the value constraint beyond type are expressed ONLY in the prose constraints beneath the diagram. Several logical schemas and the cross-cutting domain_id convention are expressed NOWHERE in this artifact, diagram or prose — they exist only as an implicit convention or external knowledge (ADR-0001, arc42) referenced from the research plan, not from this file.
